swebench_scaled_no_offload.description: Coding-agent (SWE-Bench-like) programs, no CPU offload, overloaded operating point. Paper Fig. 8 (SWE-Bench row).
swebench_scaled_no_offload.source_note: Fig. 8, Llama-3.1-8B on 1xB200 at the highest load (0.13 JPS): vLLM ~2010 s, Continuum ~1210 s -> 1.66x (70B/4xB200: ~1.68x; 8B/A100: ~1.55x; text: 'up to 2x'). Autellix/PLAS reads ~3700 s (~0.54x of vLLM); the scaled engine does NOT reproduce this PLAS degradation (PLAS ~1.0x here), so its paper reading is kept in this note rather than as a scored reference value.

delay_reduction_x.description: Reference-baseline mean program completion time divided by the method's (pooled over the experiment's traces). Headline claim of the paper (average job completion time).

p95_delay_reduction_x.description: Per-trace reference-baseline P95 completion time divided by the method's, geometric mean over traces (paper Fig. 10 tail-latency claim).

throughput_improvement_x.description: Reference-baseline drain time of a trace divided by the method's (completed programs per second ratio); paper claims 1.10x-3.22x throughput.

queue_wait_fraction.description: Constraint/cost side: total time requests wait for admission divided by total program completion time. Retaining KV that blocks other requests raises it; the paper's claim is that retention reduces per-turn queueing rather than shifting it onto other programs.

bfcl_scaled_no_offload.description: Web-search / function-calling (BFCL-like) programs, no CPU offload. Paper Fig. 8 (BFCL row).
bfcl_scaled_no_offload.source_note: Fig. 8, Llama-3.1-8B on 1xB200 at 5 JPS: vLLM ~316 s, Continuum ~213 s -> 1.48x (70B: ~1.14x; 8B/A100: ~1.33x). Autellix/PLAS ~293 s (~1.08x; engine: ~1.02x).

swebench_scaled_offload.description: Coding-agent programs with CPU offload (lost KV is reloaded instead of recomputed). Paper Figs. 9 and 10.
swebench_scaled_offload.source_note: Fig. 9, Llama-3.1-8B on 1xB200 at 0.13 JPS: vLLM ~1800 s, Continuum ~1130 s -> 1.59x; InferCept ~1650 s (~1.09x; the engine's InferCept is stronger, ~1.9-2.0x); Autellix+ ~1880 s (~0.96x; engine ~0.98x). Fig. 10 at 0.13 JPS: P90 vLLM ~2750 s vs ~1760 s -> 1.56x; P95 ~2850 s vs ~1790 s -> 1.59x.

turn_robustness_scaled.description: Coding-agent programs with 3x the turns and 1/3 the tokens per turn, CPU offload. Paper Fig. 13 (3x multiplier).
turn_robustness_scaled.source_note: Fig. 13 bar labels at the 3x multiplier (30.8 turns): vLLM 2.3x, InferCept 1.7x of Continuum's average job duration -> Continuum 2.3x over vLLM, InferCept ~1.35x over vLLM (engine's InferCept: ~2.6-3.0x, stronger than in the paper). At 5x the paper reports 3.7x.

ablation_scaled.description: Ablation (paper Fig. 15b, BFCL): program-level FCFS -> + static cold-start TTL -> full Continuum; ratios are taken against program-level FCFS.
ablation_scaled.source_note: Fig. 15(b) BFCL at 3.0 JPS: vLLM ~299 s, Program-level FCFS ~269 s, Static TTL ~226 s, Continuum ~206 s -> relative to program-level FCFS: vLLM 0.90x, Static TTL 1.19x, Continuum 1.31x. In Fig. 15(a) (SWE-Bench, high load) Static TTL and Continuum nearly coincide (~1.40x vs ~1.41x).

tool_shift_scaled.description: BFCL-like programs whose tool latencies change abruptly twice mid-trace (paper Sec. 3 motivation: tool latency varies with backend/API state). Not a paper figure; added so that tool-aware, adaptive retention is measured.
tool_shift_scaled.source_note: Benchmark extension with no paper figure. The proposed-method value is a PROXY, not a paper measurement: the Fig. 8 reading for the same program family (BFCL-like, Llama-3.1-8B/1xB200, 5 JPS: 1.48x). It only anchors the order of magnitude for the paper-consistency check.
